Proves DST-correct instant construction. The pinned `now` is `2026-03-25T12:00:00Z` (Wednesday), so in `Europe/Paris` the Monday-start week is `[2026-03-23, 2026-03-30)` — a week containing the European spring-forward transition on Sunday 2026-03-29, when Paris moves from UTC+01:00 to UTC+02:00.

The two bounds therefore sit at DIFFERENT UTC offsets: local midnight on 2026-03-23 is `2026-03-22T23:00:00Z` (+01:00), while local midnight on 2026-03-30 is `2026-03-29T22:00:00Z` (+02:00). An implementation that reads the zone offset once and applies it to both bounds — the single most common way to get this wrong — produces an upper bound one hour off, silently including or excluding an hour of rows twice a year. "Start of day" must be evaluated per date against the zone's rules at that date, not as a fixed offset for the request.
